cards.text: Big day, friend. Moses, Israel's leader, finishes setting up the tabernacle and anoints and consecrates it, with all its furnishings, the altar and all its utensils. Meanwhile I can't put together one cooling rack without three screws left over.

cards.question: The tabernacle is set up. Who comes to present an offering?
True or false: These tribal leaders are also the heads of their families.

cards.text: These are the same leaders who supervised the registration, and they bring their offering before the LORD: six covered carts and twelve oxen. Most folks show up to a housewarming with a plant, but these guys show up with a gift that has HOOVES.

cards.question: Twelve oxen and six carts. The gift works out to an ox from each leader and a cart from every ___ leaders.

cards.text: So now there are six carts and twelve oxen parked outside a tent. Then the LORD speaks to Moses.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Moses to do with the carts and oxen?

answers.text: Accept them for the Tent's work
Send them back to the leaders
Offer them on the new altar

cards.question: The LORD says to give them to the Levites. True or false: He says to split them evenly, the same for every man.

cards.text: So Moses hands the carts and oxen to the Levites, and the Gershonites, one Levite clan, get two carts and four oxen.

cards.question: Six carts in all, and the Gershonites have two. What goes to the Merarites, another Levite clan?

cards.text: That's all six carts, handed out under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. And the Kohathites, the third clan, get ZERO carts and ZERO oxen.

cards.question: Why do the Kohathites get no carts or oxen?

answers.text: They carry the holy objects on their shoulders
They camp too far from the tabernacle
They already have carts of their own

cards.text: The Kohathites: the only movers whose truck is their own shoulders. When the altar is anointed, the leaders bring offerings for its dedication and present them before the altar.

cards.question: Twelve leaders, one altar. The LORD tells Moses that each ___, one leader is to present his offering for the dedication.

cards.text: Twelve days, twelve leaders, and the EXACT same offering every time: a silver platter, a silver bowl, a gold dish of incense, and animals for burnt, sin and peace offerings. Nahshon son of Amminadab from Judah goes first, and by the end the silver alone weighs two thousand four hundred shekels. Twelve guys bring the same gift to the same party, and I bet nobody's embarrassed. I love it.
One more moment before this chapter closes. Moses goes into the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: True or false: Moses goes into the Tent of Meeting to count the silver and gold.

cards.text: He goes in to speak with the LORD, and he hears the voice speaking to him. No ringtone. No hold music. THE voice.

cards.question: Moses hears the voice from between the two ___ above the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony.

cards.text: Twelve days of silver and gold, friend, and the chapter ends with this: "Thus the LORD spoke to him."

findings.problem: Discovery questions dominate the stop. Cards 2, 3, 8, 14, 17 and 19 ask for details that earlier cards neither supply nor make inferable. For example, card 14 gives no basis for choosing day over week or month, and card 19 gives no clue about what is above the mercy seat. These go beyond the permitted few discovery questions, leaving most choices insufficiently reasoned.

rule.text:
**The check:** could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

**A few discovery questions are fine.** Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The question says "give them" and "split them" without identifying the carts and oxen. The pronoun depends on card 7, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: **Always give context in the question.** The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has four sentences, exceeding the one-to-two-sentence limit. The summary itself can remain one card, but its wording and closing reactions need to fit that limit.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has four period-ended sentences or fragments: the Bible moment followed by "No ringtone.", "No hold music." and "THE voice." That exceeds the one-to-two-sentence limit.
